observed: Real photo (scikit-image 'coffee', CC0 by Rachel Michetti): an espresso cup on a saucer with a teaspoon, on a wooden table, seen from the front and well above
Cup and saucer have the same dark red-brown glaze; the cup's inside and the top of its rim are white
The cup holds espresso with an even tan crema surface
The cup's handle is a closed loop on the front-left side, about mid-height
A stainless teaspoon lies on the saucer at the front-right; its bowl faces up and its handle runs back along the right side of the cup to beyond the saucer rim

Both rims image as ellipses: fitted to hand-picked edge points, the cup rim is 243 x 194 px centred at (292, 112) and the saucer 406 x 342 px centred at (275, 223), both nearly level (roll under 4 degrees)
inferred: Perspective camera fitted to three circles (cup rim, saucer rim, cup foot arc): 57 degrees above the table, 0.63 m away, 2.3 px RMS
Scale 0.301 mm/px from an assumed 120 mm saucer, giving a 68 mm cup rim at 54 mm height and a 55 mm foot
Cup side profile from silhouette edges at four image rows, solved through the fitted frame; left and right agree within 2 mm
Crema about 26 mm below the rim, where the far and side edges of the crema give the same radius
The spoon lies in the saucer with its handle resting on the rim (scene reading); its exact depth is not recoverable from the photo
unknowns: True size (no scale reference in the photo; a typical saucer size is assumed)
Hidden back of the cup, the underside of the saucer and the foot ring
Exact handle cross-section and the spoon's thickness
Perspective: the photo is not orthographic, so near and far edges cannot both match exactly

evidence.claim: Camera, scale, cup rim and foot
evidence.source: least-squares fit of a perspective ImageFrame to 8 cup-rim, 10 saucer-rim and 5 foot-arc edge points (fit_camera.py)
silhouette x at image rows 120, 150, 180, 200 solved for (r, z) through the frame (fit_profile.py)
